item.title: SiRPS 3.1.0
item.description:
REAPER's save dialog opens on a name you chose

Saving a new project meant typing the name at the dialog every time, so a run of shows came out named by whatever you managed at the moment of saving.

The Preferences tab now has a New project name row: a prefix for the production and a date format to pick from. Type MHET, choose 2026-09-17_1430, and REAPER's Save New Project dialog opens on MHET_2026-09-17_1430. The resolved name is shown as you set it, so it is confirmed before you apply rather than at the next save.

This is REAPER's own feature — the save-as wildcard pattern, with REAPER's own wildcards, and REAPER resolves them. The app composes the pattern and reads it back, which means the setting lives in REAPER where it belongs and keeps working whether or not you open this app again. A pattern you wrote by hand in REAPER is read back intact rather than rewritten.

Five date formats, ISO first because it is the only one that sorts into date order in Finder once a season has filled a folder. (no date) gives a plain prefix. Leave both empty and REAPER's own default is left alone.

Reports its real version

The 3.0.0 bundle told Finder it was version 0.0.0, with CFBundleVersion empty altogether. Pinning the version reached the app's own About box and update check but not the bundle PyInstaller writes around it. Both keys are stamped from the tag now, before signing.

Version history

  • 3.1.0 — REAPER's Save New Project dialog opens on a name you chose: a production prefix plus a date format, written to REAPER's own save-as wildcard pattern and previewed as you set it. The bundle reports its real version to Finder instead of 0.0.0.
  • 3.0.0 — Now SiRPS, with the suite icon. Records over MADI as well as a SoundGrid card, and you pick which ports you record to, so a second stream carrying outputs patched straight to it — program and press feeds — comes through in the same CSV. More channels resolve to their real name: Copy Audio sources count as inputs, stereo pairs by port order, the lowest-numbered channel wins a shared input, alt inputs arrive named (Oliver ALT), adjacent mono L/R pairs are dotted so Reaper makes them stereo, and older 'vM' sessions parse.

Releases before 3.0.0 predate this ledger; their notes are on the Releases page.

item.title: SiRPS 3.2.0
item.description:
Four preferences that never actually worked

Every setting in the Preferences tab wrote a key and reported success. Three of them were writing the wrong key, so REAPER was never told what you asked for — and one of the three set the opposite of what its checkbox promised.

Peak files. The peaks/ subfolder option wrote peakcachegenmode, which controls only *when* peaks are generated — on import, and on project load. Peak *location* is altpeaks &4. Worse, peakcachegenmode defaults to 3, and the code ORed bit 1 into it: 3 | 1 is 3, so the write was a no-op even on its own terms. This is the one that left .reapeaks sitting beside the audio.

Startup behaviour. loadlastproj is an enum, not a bitfield — 19 is "new project", 16 is "last active project". The code masked it (& ~1 & ~2), which turns 19 into 16. Ticking "open a new project on startup" set REAPER to reopen the last project instead.

Prompt to save on new project. Wrote saveopts &1, which is "when overwriting a project file, rename the old one to .rpp-bak". The real key is newprojdo &1. An unrelated setting was toggled instead.

Choosing a template also wrote newprojdo=1, apparently as a "use the template" flag. There is no such flag — setting newprojtmpl is what makes REAPER use it — and newprojdo is the prompt-to-save bitfield, so picking a template quietly rewrote an unrelated preference.

All four now write the documented key, and the media path and save path, which were already correct, are unchanged.

Record-arm new tracks

A new checkbox: new tracks arrive record-armed. It sets deftrackrecflags &1, bit 1 only — the same field carries the record-config dropdown in bits 16 to 128, which survive untouched.

Checkboxes tell the truth now

The four checkboxes were hardcoded to start ticked and could only ever switch a setting on, so unticking one did nothing while looking like it meant something. They now open reflecting what REAPER actually has, and toggle it either way.

A New Show Project action that actually names the project

REAPER applies its save-as wildcard pattern to the project it creates at launch, but not to File > New Project, so a show started mid-session arrives unnamed no matter what the pattern says. Nothing written to reaper.ini fixes that — it is REAPER's behaviour, not a setting.

So applying preferences now also installs SiRPS New Show Project into REAPER's Scripts folder. It reads the same pattern and save path out of REAPER's own config, shows you the resulting name to confirm or edit, then creates the dated folder, starts a new project from your template, points the media folder at Audio and saves into it.

It never touches the file dialog, which is what would have required SWS or js_ReaScriptAPI — it builds the path and saves directly. No extension needed.

Bind it once under Actions > Show action list and use it instead of File > New Project. It refuses to overwrite a project that already exists, and cancelling leaves everything untouched.

The media path now survives a project template

Setting the media folder to Audio had no effect for anyone using a project template. A template stores its own RECORD_PATH, and REAPER takes the template's over the projdefrecpath preference — so a template saved with an empty record path sent every recording to the top level of the project folder, no matter what the preference said.

It looks exactly like the media-path setting being broken, and the peaks folder compounds it: peaks nest relative to the media, so they end up at the top level too, beside the audio, rather than tucked inside it.

When a template is chosen and a media folder is set, the template's own record path is now set to match, with a .bak-.RPP copy kept beside it. A template that already agrees is left alone and no backup is written.

Version history

  • 3.2.0 — Three of the four Preferences settings were writing the wrong REAPER key and reporting success: peak location (the peaks/ subfolder), startup behaviour (which set the opposite of its checkbox), and prompt-to-save. All corrected against REAPER's documented keys. New: record-arm new tracks. The checkboxes now reflect what REAPER actually has and toggle it either way. Also installs a New Show Project ReaScript, which names a mid-session project the way REAPER only does at launch, and sets a chosen template's own record path to match the media folder, which otherwise overrides it.
  • 3.1.0 — REAPER's Save New Project dialog opens on a name you chose: a production prefix plus a date format, written to REAPER's own save-as wildcard pattern and previewed as you set it. The bundle reports its real version to Finder instead of 0.0.0.
  • 3.0.0 — Now SiRPS, with the suite icon. Records over MADI as well as a SoundGrid card, and you pick which ports you record to, so a second stream carrying outputs patched straight to it — program and press feeds — comes through in the same CSV. More channels resolve to their real name: Copy Audio sources count as inputs, stereo pairs by port order, the lowest-numbered channel wins a shared input, alt inputs arrive named (Oliver ALT), adjacent mono L/R pairs are dotted so Reaper makes them stereo, and older 'vM' sessions parse.

item.title: SiRPS 3.2.1
item.description:
Check for Updates works

In every build since it was added, Check for Updates… reported "Couldn't reach the update feed" with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED. The feed was fine; the app had nothing to check its certificate against.

HTTPS needs a bundle of trusted certificate authorities. A packaged app's OpenSSL looks for that file at a path baked in from the machine it was *built* on — a Python installation that does not exist on yours — so every secure request failed. It never showed during development, because Apple's own Python trusts the macOS keychain regardless of any file.

The app now carries its own certificate bundle and uses it for the update check. Verification is still fully on; nothing about the check was loosened.

One consequence worth knowing: because the check was broken in 3.0.0 through 3.2.0, those versions cannot tell you about this one. If you are on any of them, download 3.2.1 once from the SiRPS page — after that, updates will find you.

Version history

  • 3.2.1 — Check for Updates works. Every earlier build failed with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED because the packaged app had no certificate bundle to verify against; it now ships its own. 3.0.0–3.2.0 cannot announce this release, so download it once by hand.
  • 3.2.0 — Three of the four Preferences settings were writing the wrong REAPER key and reporting success: peak location (the peaks/ subfolder), startup behaviour (which set the opposite of its checkbox), and prompt-to-save. All corrected against REAPER's documented keys. New: record-arm new tracks. The checkboxes now reflect what REAPER actually has and toggle it either way. Also installs a New Show Project ReaScript, which names a mid-session project the way REAPER only does at launch, and sets a chosen template's own record path to match the media folder, which otherwise overrides it.

item.title: SiRPS 3.2.2
item.description:
Apply sets REAPER up properly on a fresh machine

On a machine that had never been set up, pressing Apply left REAPER reopening the last project at startup instead of starting a new one.

3.2.0 changed the Preferences checkboxes to open showing whatever REAPER already had, rather than the recommended setup. On a fresh install REAPER's own default is "reopen the last project", so the startup box opened unticked — and because Apply now sets each option both ways, Apply wrote that default straight back. The same went for prompt-to-save and the peaks subfolder.

They open ticked again, because setting REAPER up the standard way is what the app is for. Unticking one still genuinely turns it off. Record-arm new tracks is the exception: it's a personal choice rather than part of the standard setup, so it still opens on whatever REAPER has — off on a fresh install, and left on for anyone who turned it on.

Audio lands in Audio/ whatever template REAPER is using

On the same machine the peaks nested but the audio didn't, recording straight into the project folder.

A project template carries its own media path, and it overrides the preference. Apply sets the template's media path to match — but only for the template picked in the dropdown, and the dropdown recognised a template only if it lived in ProjectTemplates and its name matched loosely. A template REAPER was already using that the dropdown didn't recognise showed as "(none)", stayed in use, and was never touched, so its empty media path won.

Apply now reads back which template REAPER will actually open and aligns that one, wherever it lives. The dropdown shows it too, instead of "(none)", and matches it exactly — "Show.RPP" no longer mistakes itself for "My Show.RPP".

Apply double-checks everything, every time

Apply used to skip a setting when it already looked right, and then report what it had meant to do. Both of those trusted a single read of reaper.ini that could itself be wrong. Now:

  • Every setting is written on every Apply, whether or not it looked correct already. Nothing is skipped on the strength of a read.
  • The template is aligned on every Apply — whichever one REAPER will open, however it came to be set.
  • Everything is read back off disk afterwards, and the report lists each setting with ✓ or ✗ against what is actually there, not what was intended. If anything did not hold, the dialog says so and says why.
  • A setting that appears twice in reaper.ini is collapsed to the one value written. Before, the first copy was updated and read back as proof, while REAPER could be reading the other.
  • Apply refuses while REAPER is running. REAPER keeps its preferences in memory and writes them all back when it quits, which silently undoes anything written meanwhile — the most likely reason a setting "doesn't stick". This was only checked when SiRPS opened, so launching REAPER afterwards went unnoticed.

Version history

Audio lands in Audio/ whatever template REAPER is using, including one outside ProjectTemplates. Apply now writes every setting and the template every time, reads them all back off disk, reports ✓/✗ per setting, and refuses while REAPER is running.
  • 3.2.1 — Check for Updates works. Every earlier build failed with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED because the packaged app had no certificate bundle to verify against; it now ships its own. 3.0.0–3.2.0 cannot announce this release, so download it once by hand.
  • 3.2.0 — Three of the four Preferences settings were writing the wrong REAPER key and reporting success: peak location (the peaks/ subfolder), startup behaviour (which set the opposite of its checkbox), and prompt-to-save. All corrected against REAPER's documented keys. New: record-arm new tracks. The checkboxes now reflect what REAPER actually has and toggle it either way. Also installs a New Show Project ReaScript, which names a mid-session project the way REAPER only does at launch, and sets a chosen template's own record path to match the media folder, which otherwise overrides it.
  • 3.1.0 — REAPER's Save New Project dialog opens on a name you chose: a production prefix plus a date format, written to REAPER's own save-as wildcard pattern and previewed as you set it. The bundle reports its real version to Finder instead of 0.0.0.
  • 3.0.0 — Now SiRPS, with the suite icon. Records over MADI as well as a SoundGrid card, and you pick which ports you record to, so a second stream carrying outputs patched straight to it — program and press feeds — comes through in the same CSV. item.title: SiRPS 3.2.3
item.description:
One project backup, not one per save

A two-hour recording left 54 project backup files in its folder — one .rpp-bak for every save, each with its own timestamp.

That comes from three of REAPER's own defaults working together: auto-save every minute, auto-save any time (including while recording), and "timestamp backup", which makes each backup a new file instead of replacing the last one.

A new Preferences option, on by default, keeps one rolling backup: a single .rpp-bak of the previous save, overwritten each time. Auto-save is left exactly as it was — still every minute, still during recording — so a crash mid-show is covered just as before. Only the pile of files goes.

Untick it to go back to a timestamped file on every save.
